sentences.text: Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 7571 of 2023

Petitioner :- Tejpal @ Bholu
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Petitioner :- Munesh Kumar Upadhyay,Sheetla Prasad Gound
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Balwant Singh
Hon'ble Vivek Kumar Birla,J.
Hon'ble Rajendra Kumar-IV,J.
1.

Heard Sri Sunil Kumar holding brief of Sri M.K. Upadhyay, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri
Balwant Singh, learned counsel appearing for the informant and Sri Ratan Singh, learned A.G.A for
the State respondents.
2.  The relief sought in this petition is for quashing of the F.I.R. dated 22.2.2023 registered as Case Crime No. 200 of 2023 under Sections 376 IPC, Police Station Highway, District Mathura.
Further prayer has been made not to arrest the petitioner in the aforesaid case.

3. By drawing attention to paragraphs 6, 7, 11 and 12 of the writ petition submission of learned counsel for the petitioner is that the first information report is based on absolutely false allegations and no such incident had taken place.

It is next submitted that the petitioner is aged about 40 years Tejpal @ Bholu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73932618/
1 and the victim is married lady having three children and the petitioner had business / professional term with the husband of victim and no offence has been committed by the petitioner.

entities.text: Tejpal @ Bholu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the informant and learned AGA opposed the prayer for quashing of the FIR, which discloses cognizable offence.
Learned A.G.A. further submits that in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. the victim has supported the prosecution version.
5. We also find that the grounds that are being taken by learned counsel for the petitioner are the defence of the petitioner.
6. Perusal of the impugned first information report prima facie reveals commission of cognizable offence.

Therefore, in view of the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana and others vs. Bhajan Lal and others, 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335 and M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2021 SC 1918 and in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.3262/2021 (Leelavati Devi @ Leelawati & another vs. the State of Uttar Pradesh) decided on 07.10.2021, no case has been made out for interference with the impugned first information report.

sentences.text: 7. Therefore, the writ petition is dismissed leaving it open for the petitioner to apply before the competent court for anticipatory bail/bail as permissible under law and in accordance with law.
